claim: An emergency fund is a cash reserve specifically set aside for unexpected expenses or financial emergencies.
CFPB guidance says the amount to set aside for emergencies depends on the household situation and past unexpected expenses, rather than imposing one universal amount.
CFPB describes safe, accessible storage as important characteristics for emergency savings.
Cash flow includes the timing of income and expenses; mismatched timing can create temporary shortages.
CFPB describes automatic recurring transfers as a way to save consistently but warns that insufficient checking-account funds can incur overdraft fees.
CFPB suggests setting a specific savings goal and monitoring progress to support a saving habit.
CFPB observational data show differences in credit, debt, bill-paying difficulty, and well-being by reported emergency-savings levels, without establishing causality.
population: US consumers with credit bureau records

claim: In CFPB app data, guaranteed saving rules such as payday saving were associated with greater accumulation than spending-contingent rules; this is observational.
Federal Reserve 2025 survey reports that 30% of US adults had income varying at least occasionally, and 11% said variation created difficulty paying bills in the prior year.
Annual income totals can obscure month-to-month volatility and timing mismatches that cause financial challenges.
In the Fed 2025 survey, 63% of adults ages 18–29 reported doing okay or living comfortably financially; this is descriptive US survey data.
World Bank Global Findex 2025 uses 2024 survey data on roughly 148,000 adults across 141 economies.
CFPB guidance says US credit-card minimum payments must be made by the due date to avoid late-payment consequences, subject to contract terms.
Paying more than the card minimum generally reduces interest cost and shortens payoff time.
Many US card issuers accrue credit-card interest daily, and earlier principal payments can reduce interest when interest is accruing.
limitations: Many, not all, card issuers; exact APR and grace period vary

claim: US card issuers generally allocate above-minimum payments first to the highest-APR sub-balance on a card.
population: US cardholders with multiple APR categories
limitations: US issuer rules and card terms apply

claim: When a US cardholder cannot pay the required minimum, CFPB recommends contacting the card issuer immediately to discuss options.
population: Consumers unable to pay card bills
limitations: Hardship programs vary by creditor and borrower

claim: CFPB identifies nonprofit credit counseling as a possible support option and cautions about some debt-settlement firm practices.
population: Consumers unable to pay card bills
limitations: Hardship programs vary by creditor and borrower

claim: A US three-year repayment disclosure assumes no further spending; paying only minimums can extend payoff for years.
A deferred-interest card offer may charge interest if the promotional balance is not repaid by the offer deadline; exact offer terms require checking.
CFPB survey analysis finds that respondents who report not saving are more likely to have had trouble paying bills, an association not an effect estimate.
A 2022 meta-analysis of 76 randomized experiments involving over 160,000 people found positive average effects of financial education on knowledge and downstream financial behaviors.
A meta-analysis of 126 studies finds heterogeneous financial education effects; debt behavior is comparatively difficult to change and teachable-moment delivery is associated with stronger effects.
A field study and experiments suggest concentrating repayments in one account can increase debt-payoff motivation, especially for smaller accounts.
limitations: Motivation effect not same as lowest interest cost

claim: SEC Investor.gov says investment asset allocation depends on time horizon and tolerance of investment risk.
Diversification spreads investments to reduce concentration risk, but narrowly focused funds need not provide broad diversification.
SEC Investor.gov recommends checking total purchase/sale costs and ongoing investment fees before investing.
The UK multi-criteria analysis manual presents MCDA as a structured method for evaluating options using multiple criteria; it does not supply FinAgent-specific weights.
limitations: Method justifies framework, not numerical FinAgent weights

claim: European Commission JRC research identifies conceptual pitfalls in interpreting composite-indicator weights.

population: Third-party DPC lenders and UK consumers
